_about: Field terms for F204, same shape as papers/glossary.json.

metamorphic-testing.definition: testing a program by checking a relation that must hold between the outputs of several related runs, used when no trusted expected output is available
metamorphic-testing.excludes: a test that compares one output with a stored expected value, and any proof that an output is correct

adjoint.definition: the partner of a linear map that carries vectors from the output space back to the input space so that the inner product of an output with a vector equals the inner product of the input with the partner's result
adjoint.excludes: the inverse, which undoes the map; an adjoint exists for maps that cannot be undone

mutant.definition: a copy of a program with one small fault planted by rule, such as a plus swapped for a minus, used to measure whether a test notices
mutant.excludes: a bug written by a person; mutants stand in for such bugs and may not resemble them

equivalent-mutant.definition: a mutant whose change leaves the program's behaviour the same on every input, so that no test can or should fail on it
equivalent-mutant.excludes: a fault that a weak test happens to miss

differential-oracle.definition: a judge of behaviour that runs two versions of a program on the same inputs and reports whether their outputs differ; here it marks a mutant as a fault when it differs from the original on random inputs
differential-oracle.excludes: any statement that the original program is right

calibration-point.definition: a single forward test case with a known closed-form answer, standing for the one check a new instrument model often gets
calibration-point.excludes: a calibration of hardware against a physical standard

wide-forward.definition: a set of 4 to 15 forward test cases with closed-form answers at random parameter values, all of which must pass
wide-forward.excludes: any check that runs the model backward or against a complement, and any reference taken from measurement

backward-check.definition: a test that runs an instrument model in reverse against itself, by time reversal, reciprocity, an adjoint identity or an inverse, and needs no reference value
backward-check.excludes: a comparison with a known answer

contrary-check.definition: a test that runs an instrument model against its opposite or complement, such as an aperture and its complementary screen or a lens and its negative, and needs no reference value
contrary-check.excludes: a comparison with a known answer, and the backward check, which reverses the same case

three-way.definition: the backward and contrary checks taken together after a forward calibration; a fault is caught three-way when either check fails
three-way.excludes: the wide forward test, which is scored apart

false-pass.definition: a planted fault, confirmed by the differential oracle, that still passes the calibration point
false-pass.excludes: equivalent mutants, and mutants that crash a test

sign-flip.definition: a paired test that gives each difference a random sign many times and counts how often the mean of the re-signed differences reaches the real mean
sign-flip.excludes: a test that assumes a normal distribution, and any comparison of unpaired groups

benjamini-hochberg.definition: an adjustment of a family of p values that limits the expected share of false discoveries among the tests called significant
benjamini-hochberg.excludes: control of the chance of any single false discovery, which is the stricter Bonferroni aim

compensating-pair.definition: two planted faults in one function, drawn at random, kept in the score when together they still pass the calibration point
compensating-pair.excludes: pairs chosen by hand to cancel
